---
title: "Versioning Docs"
---

Each version is one rendered site, kept in its own directory. The current
render is also copied to the deployment site root. Historical directories
stay as they were. Paths below are relative to that site root, not the domain
root: the same manifest works at `/` and a repository prefix such as `/askr/`.

```text
/                         current release
/v0.3.0/                  immutable 0.3.0 site
/askr-versions.json       one version-list authority
```

Put `askr-versions.json` at the rendered site's root and include it in
`project.resources`:

```json
{
  "mode": "inline",
  "versions": [
    {"label": "0.4.2", "root": "/", "latest": true},
    {"label": "0.3.0", "root": "/v0.3.0/"}
  ]
}
```

Askr locates the manifest from Quarto's page offset. Each `root` is a version
directory relative to that deployment root; `/` selects the current site.
Use `href` instead of `root` for a fixed destination. Relative or leading-slash
hrefs are site-relative; absolute URLs keep their origin. Fixed destinations
do not preserve the current page.

`inline` prints the version beside a short title. `title` shows the title and
chevron, with the number only in the menu. Try the
[long-title specimen](versions.html?askr-version-mode=title). Its `longTitle`
manifest entry is only a gallery specimen, not required consumer configuration.

Existing consumers can still supply an inline
`<script id="askr-versions" type="application/json">` when an external
manifest is unavailable. Use one authority, not duplicated external and inline
lists. This gallery uses only the external JSON.

## Keyboard interaction

The selector is a disclosure, not a listbox. Tab to its button, then press
Enter or Space to open it. Tab and Shift-Tab move through ordinary links;
Enter follows one. Escape closes it and returns focus to the button. Tabbing
away or clicking outside closes it without moving outside focus back.
The current version link has `aria-current="true"`.

## Corresponding pages and missing pages

The menu retains the current page path, query and fragment when switching
between `root` entries. From `/askr/usage/versions.html`, 0.3.0 points to
`/askr/v0.3.0/usage/versions.html`, not `/v0.3.0/askr/usage/versions.html`.

For an ordinary same-origin click, Askr checks the destination. A 404 sends
the reader to that selected version's manifest root. Network errors retain
the original destination, rather than inventing a page. Modified clicks
(Cmd/Ctrl-click or a new tab) and external URLs retain browser link behavior;
the host's error page owns those cases. Projects own their hosting error page.

This gallery supplies `404.qmd`, deriving its deployment root from Quarto's
rendered offset and matching the external manifest. Existing historical
snapshots keep their original scripts and version lists: a new Askr install
does not rewrite an old rendered site.

Open this page and select 0.3.0. This page is absent from that snapshot, so
the current selector takes you to its home. That historical gallery retains
its original Install area rather than this site's Usage area.

## Publishing

1. Render the exact tag being frozen.
2. Copy that rendered site into its version directory.
3. Publish the current rendered site at the deployment root.
4. Update the one version manifest.

Keep historical directories unchanged. A version number is a source identity;
it does not itself prove that deployment has finished.
